Users edit lists on their phones, sometimes without a connection, and expect changes to appear on teammates' devices as soon as they reconnect. Each task has different optional fields that the product team keeps changing. Which database fits best?

choices.text: BigQuery, a data warehouse that stores each task update as a row for later analysis with SQL
Firestore, a serverless document database with real-time synchronization and offline support for mobile and web apps
Cloud SQL, a managed relational database that requires a fixed table design defined in advance for every task field and each change
Spanner, a globally consistent relational database for banking-style transactions across regions

stem: A national retailer has ten years of sales, loyalty and web-traffic history, many terabytes in total. Business analysts, who know SQL, want to run complex aggregate reports across all of it, such as revenue by region and product over time. The company does not want to size, tune or maintain database servers. Which service should hold and analyze this data?

choices.text: BigQuery, because it is a serverless data warehouse that analyzes very large datasets with SQL and no servers to manage
Cloud SQL, because analysts can query the whole ten-year history from one managed relational instance that the team sizes and tunes
Bigtable, because key-based lookups on a single sales row return in milliseconds
Firestore, because documents can store each sales record with a flexible set of fields

stem: A new executive asks the data team to explain the difference between relational and non-relational databases in plain terms. Which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A non-relational (NoSQL) database cannot scale beyond one server and is used only for small applications
A non-relational database requires the same fixed table design as a relational one, only with different software
A non-relational database can store data as documents, key-value pairs or wide columns, often with a flexible schema
A relational database is a type of object storage that keeps each row as a separate file
A relational database stores data in tables with defined relationships and is queried with SQL

stem: A news agency stores millions of photos, video clips and PDF press releases. Reporters upload files from anywhere, editors need to fetch each file by name, and the agency wants capacity that grows without planning and is billed for what it keeps. Nobody needs to run SQL over the files. Which description explains why Cloud Storage suits this need?

choices.text: It is object storage that holds each file as an object in a bucket and scales without capacity planning
It is a relational database that splits each photo into rows and columns for joins
It is a data warehouse that loads every video into a table so that analysts can aggregate frames with SQL
It is a document database that keeps each press release as a JSON record with a flexible set of fields

stem: A company moved last year's customer-support recordings to Archive storage to save money. This quarter the compliance team began reviewing the recordings every week, and the storage bill went up instead of down. What explains the result?

choices.text: Archive storage is a zonal class, so the weekly reviews are charged a cross-region transfer fee each time
Archive storage cannot be read at all until the objects are first moved back to Standard storage
Archive storage costs more per stored gigabyte than Standard storage once data is a year old
Archive is meant for data read less than once a year, so frequent reads add access costs that outweigh savings

stem: A machine learning team trains models on a very large image dataset. The training cluster runs in a single zone, and the team has found that data loading from storage is the bottleneck, leaving expensive accelerators idle. The team wants storage placed in the same zone as the cluster for the lowest possible latency. Which Cloud Storage option is designed for this?

choices.text: Archive storage in a multi-region bucket, which gives the lowest storage cost for large datasets
Coldline storage in a dual-region bucket, which keeps a copy of the data in two regions
Rapid storage in a zonal bucket, which is optimized for I/O-intensive workloads next to compute
Nearline storage with Autoclass enabled, which moves unread data into colder classes over time

stem: A regional bank runs a self-managed MySQL database in its own data center. The hardware lease ends in six months. The bank wants to move to a managed Google Cloud database, keep the application running during the move, and switch over with as little downtime as possible. Which Google Cloud service is designed to help?

choices.text: Looker, which models data so that business users can build dashboards on the old database
Database Migration Service, which handles the initial snapshot and ongoing replication to Cloud SQL for MySQL
Cloud Storage Autoclass, which moves database files between storage classes during the migration
Pub/Sub, which broadcasts each database row as a message that other systems can subscribe to

stem: A mid-sized insurer runs several self-managed databases on virtual machines in its own data center. Its administrators spend most of their week on patching, backups and failover tests. Leadership wants to modernize by moving to managed database services. Which TWO benefits should leadership expect? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Capacity can be adjusted to demand, without buying and installing new hardware for peak load
The insurer gains full control of the physical servers and operating system that run each database
Every application can run unchanged on any managed database, whatever engine it was written for
The insurer is released from all responsibility for who can access its data and how it is classified
Google takes over routine tasks such as backups, patching and failover so staff can focus on applications and data

stem: A small consultancy and a global payments company each need a new relational database. The consultancy's internal tool will serve a few hundred users in one region. The payments company must process transactions from customers on several continents with strong consistency and near-continuous availability. Which pairing of products is the most appropriate?

choices.text: Spanner for the consultancy and Cloud SQL for the payments company
Cloud SQL for the consultancy and Spanner for the payments company
Bigtable for the consultancy and Firestore for the payments company
BigQuery for the consultancy and Cloud Storage for the payments company

stem: A retail company has a central data warehouse, but only a small team of analysts can pull answers from it. Store managers, buyers and marketers wait days for reports, and each department defines "net sales" differently. Leadership wants every employee to explore trusted data on their own, using one shared definition of each metric. Which Google Cloud product addresses this?

choices.text: Spanner, to move the whole data warehouse into a transactional database that every employee can query directly
Pub/Sub, to send each employee a message every time a sales record is created
Cloud Storage, to give every employee access to the raw files that the warehouse is built from
Looker, a BI platform with a semantic layer that sets governed metric definitions for self-service use

stem: A food-delivery company wants its operations team to watch orders, courier locations and delivery delays on a wall dashboard that updates within seconds, so dispatchers can reassign orders before customers complain. Which combination is the most direct way to deliver this?

choices.text: Firestore to store courier data and Dataflow to print a daily summary for dispatchers
Cloud SQL to store all events and a monthly email report generated by an analyst
BigQuery to analyze the continuously arriving data and Looker to present it as live dashboards
Cloud Storage Archive to keep the order events and Spanner to render them on the dashboard

stem: A credit-card company reviews transactions for fraud in a nightly batch job. Fraudsters often make many purchases within minutes, so most losses happen before the next morning's review. Executives ask why the company should invest in real-time streaming analytics. Which TWO statements describe the value? (Select TWO)

choices.text: It lets the company drop historical data, because fraud decisions depend on the most recent transaction alone
Responses can be based on current data, such as blocking a card or alerting the cardholder at that moment
It depends on copying the transaction data into a spreadsheet each night so that analysts can review it
It prevents fraudulent transactions from being approved, so the company can retire its fraud review process
Each event is evaluated as it arrives, so suspicious activity can be flagged and acted on in seconds rather than hours

stem: A smart-home company has millions of thermostats that send readings continuously. Several teams, such as billing, energy forecasting and device support, each need to consume these readings, and engineers do not want the thermostats to depend on any team's systems being online. Which service decouples the senders from the consumers?

choices.text: Cloud Storage Coldline, a low-cost class that keeps readings for long-term retention
Cloud SQL, a relational database that every team queries directly whenever it needs the latest thermostat reading
Looker, a business intelligence platform that visualizes the readings in dashboards
Pub/Sub, a messaging service where publishers send events to a topic and subscribers receive them

stem: A media company receives clickstream events through a messaging service. It needs to clean the events, remove duplicates, enrich them with customer information and load them into BigQuery, both for a continuous stream and for large historical files. The team wants a fully managed service that scales automatically with the volume and does not require managing servers. Which service fits?

choices.text: Dataflow, a managed service that runs batch and streaming data pipelines and autoscales its workers
Cloud Storage Nearline, a storage class that deduplicates and enriches the files it holds
Firestore, a document database that transforms events as they are written into collections
Looker, a BI platform that cleans and loads data by letting analysts drag fields onto a dashboard

stem: A bank has hundreds of existing data-processing jobs written for Apache Spark and Hadoop that run on its own cluster. Contracts for the hardware end soon. Leadership wants to move these jobs to Google Cloud quickly, keep the open source tools the engineers already know, and avoid paying for an idle cluster between runs. Which Google Cloud service fits?

choices.text: Cloud SQL, which runs Spark code inside the relational engine
Pub/Sub, which executes the jobs on a schedule after each message arrives
Managed Service for Apache Spark, which runs open source Spark and Hadoop jobs on clusters started and stopped on demand
Looker, which automatically rewrites the existing Spark code into dashboards that business users can open and share

stem: A company has two data projects. Project one is a new pipeline that must process events from a message stream and also handle historical files, with no servers to manage. Project two is a set of existing Spark jobs that engineers want to move without rewriting. Which TWO statements about choosing services are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Managed Service for Apache Spark suits project one because it cannot run existing code, which forces a new design
Managed Service for Apache Spark suits project two because it runs open source Spark jobs with little redevelopment
Pub/Sub suits project two because it is the engine that runs Spark programs
Dataflow suits project two because it executes unmodified Spark programs directly without any translation
Dataflow suits project one because it is fully managed, autoscaling and handles both streaming and batch

stem: An energy utility wants to build an end-to-end solution. Smart meters send readings continuously. The readings must be received reliably, cleaned and aggregated as they arrive, stored for SQL analysis, and shown to managers in dashboards. Which sequence matches the role of each service?

choices.text: Pub/Sub receives the readings, Dataflow cleans them, BigQuery stores them for SQL analysis, Looker presents dashboards
Looker receives the readings, Pub/Sub cleans them, BigQuery presents the dashboards, Dataflow stores them for SQL analysis
BigQuery receives the readings, Looker cleans them, Dataflow stores them, Pub/Sub presents the dashboards
Dataflow receives the readings, Looker cleans them, Pub/Sub stores them, BigQuery presents the dashboards

stem: A regional insurer must add automatic transcription of recorded phone claims to its claims portal before the busy season starts in six weeks. Transcription is a common task, the insurer has no machine learning staff, and the transcripts do not need to be a source of competitive advantage. Which approach best fits these strategic factors?

choices.text: Train a custom speech model from scratch on the insurer's recordings, because only a self-built model can ever be considered accurate
Hire a research team to design a new model architecture first, then decide later whether the portal needs transcription at all
Wait for the busy season to end and then fund a multi-year programme that builds a general-purpose speech platform in-house
Call a pre-trained speech API such as Speech-to-Text, which delivers the capability quickly with little development effort or ML expertise

stem: A specialty lender holds fifteen years of its own repayment histories and believes that a model trained on this data would predict defaults better than any competitor's generic tool. Leadership accepts a longer project to gain an advantage that rivals cannot copy. Which factor most strongly argues for a custom model on Agent Platform rather than a ready-made API?

choices.text: Reduced expertise, because custom training on proprietary data removes any need for data preparation or for evaluating results
Speed, because training a custom model always finishes faster than calling a service that already exists and is ready to use
Differentiation, because a model trained on proprietary data can capture patterns that a generic pre-trained service cannot offer to competitors
Uniformity, because every competitor using the same generic service would then get identical predictions, which the lender prefers because it makes outcomes easy to compare

stem: A mail-order retailer keeps customer purchase records in tables. It wants to predict which customers are likely to stop buying, but it has no data scientists and no one who writes training code. The retailer is willing to prepare a labelled dataset. Which Google Cloud approach fits best?

choices.text: AutoML on Agent Platform, which trains a prediction model from labelled tabular data without requiring code or deep data-science skills
Speech-to-Text, which converts customer call audio into text transcripts but does not train on purchase records or make predictions
Cloud Translation, which converts the text of customer messages from one language to another but does not predict behaviour
Custom training on Agent Platform, in which engineers write a training application and choose algorithms, loss functions and hardware

stem: A grocery chain's data lives in BigQuery. Its analysts are fluent in SQL but do not program in Python or Java, and they want to forecast weekly demand per store without waiting for the engineering team. Which Google Cloud capability fits?

choices.text: BigQuery ML, which lets analysts create and run forecasting models with GoogleSQL statements in the warehouse
A custom training job on dedicated accelerators, where engineers package a Python training application that reads the tables
Cloud Translation, a pre-trained language API that converts text between languages and does no numeric forecasting
Export the BigQuery tables to spreadsheets, and have each analyst write a forecasting program in Python or Java

stem: A data-platform director wants to justify BigQuery ML to the board. Which TWO benefits can she cite? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Every model type is available with unlimited control over the training hardware, including the choice of individual accelerators
Models are built where the data already sits, so there is no need to move and reformat large datasets for separate ML tools
Models trained in BigQuery ML automatically replace all dashboards, removing the need for any business intelligence tools
Warehouse data is first copied into a separate ML platform, and the models are returned to BigQuery after a manual review
Data analysts can build and run models with SQL skills they already have, without writing Python or Java ML code

stem: A global furniture seller wants its support site to show product manuals and customer notices in the shopper's own language. The content changes weekly and the seller wants the least possible build effort. Which Google Cloud AI service matches?

choices.text: Speech-to-Text, a pre-trained service that turns spoken audio into text but does not render written content in other languages
AutoML tabular training, which builds prediction models from labelled rows and columns and has no function for converting languages
Cloud Vision, a pre-trained service that analyses images to detect labels and text but does not translate written content
Cloud Translation, a pre-trained service that translates text and documents between many languages through an API

stem: A used-car marketplace receives photographs from sellers and wants to automatically read licence-plate text and flag photos that contain unwanted content before publishing. The team wants a ready-made capability, not a model project. Which service fits best?

choices.text: BigQuery ML time-series forecasting, which predicts future numeric values and does not analyse photographs
Cloud Translation API, which converts text from one language to another but does not analyse the content of photographs
Cloud Vision API, which analyses images with pre-trained models to detect text, labels and explicit content
Speech-to-Text, which transcribes audio recordings and cannot examine the pixels of an uploaded photograph

stem: A hotel group's front desk wants one assistant that can read a guest's typed question, look at a photo of a damaged item the guest sends, and draft a polite written reply. Which kind of Google Cloud AI is the best match for this mix of inputs and outputs?

choices.text: A multimodal foundation model such as Gemini, which can understand text and images together and generate written responses
A translation-only API, which converts text between languages but cannot interpret photographs or compose new messages
A speech-only API, which transcribes audio but cannot interpret typed questions or photographs
A tabular AutoML model, which predicts one outcome from labelled rows and does not write replies

stem: A chief information officer asks colleagues to explain, in one sentence, what Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform offers a company that wants to use AI on Google Cloud. Which description is most accurate?

choices.text: A physical data-centre appliance that runs on the customer's premises and cannot be reached from any Google Cloud service
A single prebuilt application for answering employees' e-mail, with no way to choose models or to build anything custom
A spreadsheet add-on for formatting cells that is sold separately from other Google Cloud products and has no model catalogue or ML tooling
A managed platform to find and use models, build and deploy agents and apps, and train and manage custom ML models across their lifecycle

stem: A product manager at a publisher wants to try out different instructions and models for a summarising feature, and wants to share working prototypes with colleagues who do not write code. Which Agent Platform tool suits this?

choices.text: A data-warehouse export job, which copies tables to cloud storage but does not provide any way to prototype with models
Agent Studio, which provides a low-code environment for designing and prototyping with models and agents without writing code
A hardware reservation for accelerator clusters, which provides computing capacity but no way to design or share prototypes
A raw training cluster for custom models, which requires engineers to write and run a training application first

stem: A manufacturer must classify photos of its own parts as "pass" or "defect". Option one is AutoML with labelled photos from its production line; option two is custom training by a small ML engineering team. The classification goal is standard and the team is small, but later it may want a special loss function. Which comparison guides the decision best?

choices.text: AutoML can target any objective and supply any loss function, so custom training is never needed for any business problem
Custom training is faster and needs no expertise, while AutoML requires its users to write their own training application and algorithms
AutoML and custom training differ only in price, since both need an identical amount of expertise, code and time to produce a first model
AutoML gets a model faster with less expertise but only for predefined objectives, while custom training allows any objective at greater effort

stem: A media group wants a summarising feature, but its leadership worries about depending on a single model supplier: the best model for this task may change within a year, and the group wants to switch without rebuilding the application. Which strategic factor and Google Cloud capability address this?

choices.text: Choice and flexibility, using Model Garden on Agent Platform to try and switch among Google, partner and open models
Differentiation, by fine-tuning one chosen supplier's model on the group's archive so its summaries stand out
Implementation speed, by adopting the first available model through its supplier's own API to launch quickly
Technical expertise, by hiring a data science team to build and train the group's own summarising model from scratch

stem: A regional clinic wants to turn recorded dictation into text notes. A consultant proposes first buying a large cluster of accelerators on AI Hypercomputer so that the clinic can train its own speech model. The clinic has no ML staff and no wish to compete on speech technology. What is the soundest advice?

choices.text: Use a pre-trained speech API first; AI Hypercomputer is for organizations that train and serve large models themselves and need that scale
Cancel the project, because dictation transcription cannot be done on Google Cloud without training a model
Proceed with the cluster, because any AI workload on Google Cloud must run on AI Hypercomputer before an API can be called
Proceed with the cluster, because training a speech model internally is always faster than calling an existing service

stem: A marketing agency is choosing how to get product-description writing. One idea is to call Gemini with carefully written instructions. Another is to train a language model. The agency has few examples, a two-week deadline and needs good-enough quality. Which TWO statements are the sound reasoning? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Prompt-based use rules out ever improving quality afterwards, because a foundation model cannot be adapted to a specific business task
Training a language model from scratch is the quickest option because it removes any need for large datasets or computing power
A foundation model can be steered by prompts, which is the quickest route and needs no training data or model-building skills
Choosing a foundation model removes the agency's choice of models, because the platform contains only a single model
If prompting later falls short, tuning on its own examples can raise quality for the specific task, so the agency can escalate when needed

stem: Nine months ago an airline began building its own translation model for customer notices. The project is late, needs constant maintenance, and quality is no better than commercial services. Notices are ordinary written text, and the airline wants service restored quickly. What should leadership conclude?

choices.text: Translation requires a speech model, so the project should switch to Speech-to-Text before any further investment
The task is a commodity, so adopting Cloud Translation would have given faster results with far less effort and expertise
The airline should add a second custom model for the same task, since two models always cost less than one managed API
The team needs more training data and more accelerators, because a custom model is always the correct choice for translation

stem: A food manufacturer used a pre-trained image service to inspect photos of its own packaging line. The service labels general objects correctly but cannot tell the company's specific seal faults apart. The company has thousands of labelled photos of those faults. What is the best next step?

choices.text: Stop using AI for inspection and ask suppliers to describe each fault in written reports that the quality team reads
Replace the image service with Cloud Translation so that the fault names are standardized across languages
Train a custom image model on the labelled fault photos, for example with AutoML on Agent Platform, to learn the plant's specific defects
Keep relying on the generic service and add more people to review every photo it labels by hand

stem: A utility's contact centre records thousands of calls a day. Managers want searchable text of each call and a short summary of the customer's issue. Which combination of Google Cloud AI offerings fits?

choices.text: Speech-to-Text to turn the audio into transcripts, then a Gemini model to summarize each transcript into the customer's issue
Cloud Vision API to read the audio files as images, then Cloud Translation to shorten the readable text into a summary
Gemini alone, with the audio discarded after each call so that only the managers' own written notes are summarized
BigQuery ML forecasting to turn the audio into text, then AutoML tabular training to write the summary of each call

stem: A national retailer wants analysts to classify thousands of customer reviews stored in BigQuery as positive, neutral or negative and then report counts by product, using the skills the analysts already have. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Build and host a new custom language model on dedicated accelerators before any analysis can begin
Export the reviews into e-mail attachments and have managers read and tag each review by hand every month
Use Cloud Translation to convert the reviews into another language, since translation also scores the feelings in the text
Use BigQuery ML from SQL to call a Gemini model or a Cloud AI API over the review text and store results in a table

stem: A bank's data-science group wants one governed environment to prepare datasets, train custom models, deploy them to production and keep them under control, plus a catalogue of ready models to try. Which TWO capabilities of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform match this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A physical branch network of ATMs that dispenses cash, with no connection to model building or governance
Managed datasets with AutoML and custom training, so the group can build models from its own data and manage them across their lifecycle
A billing statement printer that formats invoices, which is unrelated to datasets, models or deployment tooling
A consumer photo-sharing service for uploading holiday pictures, with no tools for datasets, training or deployment
Model Garden, a library to discover, test and deploy Google, partner and open models without leaving the platform

stem: A retailer has three AI requests: (1) a forecast of weekly store demand from warehouse tables, built by SQL-fluent analysts; (2) captions for product photos with no training project; (3) a model for a unique, patented sorting objective needing its own loss function. Which pairing is the best fit?

choices.text: AutoML for the patented objective, because AutoML can target any objective that a company can describe in writing
A pre-trained translation API for all three requests, since one service is simpler to explain to the board
Custom training for the forecast, BigQuery ML for the photo captions, and a pre-trained service for the patented sorting objective as well
BigQuery ML for the forecast, a pre-trained vision or Gemini service for captions, and custom training on Agent Platform for the unique objective

stem: A manufacturer must leave its data center this year. Its production-planning software is a vendor package that needs a specific operating system, a licensed agent and administrator access to the machine, and the vendor will not support a rewrite. Which Google Cloud product gives the manufacturer the fastest path with the least change to the software?

choices.text: Cloud Run functions, which runs small pieces of event-driven code that Google invokes with no operating system choice
Apigee, which publishes and secures APIs in front of backend services but does not host the vendor package itself
Compute Engine, which runs VMs where the company picks the operating system and keeps administrator control
Cloud Run, which runs stateless containers that scale with requests and hide the operating system from the application owner

stem: A finance firm's risk team runs workloads of very different sizes. Some need many CPUs but little memory, others need large memory, and one team wants GPUs for model training. Leadership wants to avoid buying fixed server models. Which TWO statements describe the business value Compute Engine offers here? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Teams can choose from predefined machine types or define custom machine configurations, so each workload gets a size that fits it
Google patches and upgrades the software inside each customer VM automatically, so the risk team never administers guest operating systems
Every VM is automatically converted into a container, so the team no longer needs to think about machine sizes
Compute Engine requires committing to a fixed server model for several years, so capacity planning is simplified
Machine types for modern workloads include options with GPUs and TPUs, so AI and ML jobs run on the same infrastructure family as other VMs

stem: An airline's booking software is one large application. Changing the baggage-fee rules forces a full release of everything, so new features reach customers only twice a year. The CTO wants features released independently and failures in one area not to bring down the rest. What business value does a microservices architecture offer for this goal?

choices.text: The application becomes a single deployable unit, so there is only one release to test and one place where a failure can occur
Each capability is released and scaled on its own schedule, so features ship faster and a fault stays in one service
The number of teams needed falls to one, because a single group must own every service to keep them consistent
Hardware is no longer needed to run the application, because services are described as code and run without any compute resources at all

stem: A startup's three developers want to launch a customer-facing app within weeks. They would rather not build their own database operations, authentication and messaging systems. Which TWO statements describe how managed services accelerate this goal? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Managed services remove the need to design the application, because Google chooses the business logic on the startup's behalf
Managed services guarantee that the startup will never pay for any resource, because Google absorbs the operating costs
Google runs the underlying operations such as patching, backups and scaling, so developers spend their time on features rather than plumbing
Managed services are only available for workloads that are first rewritten as VMs with the startup's own operating system images
Developers can combine ready-made services for data, messaging and runtime, so the team assembles the app instead of building every part itself

stem: A ticket retailer buys enough servers to survive a once-a-year sale, so most of the year the hardware sits mostly idle. The CFO wants spending to follow demand while the site still copes with the peak. Which modern application development approach addresses both goals?

choices.text: Run on elastic managed platforms that scale out when traffic rises and scale back when it falls, so cost follows actual use
Move the application to one very large server, so that only a single machine has to be paid for, patched and monitored
Provision the peak capacity permanently on virtual machines, so that the site never has to scale and cost stays predictable
Cap traffic at the average level during the sale, so that the existing servers are enough and no extra capacity is ever needed

stem: A logistics company has packaged dozens of services as containers. Its engineers want Kubernetes features such as rolling updates and automatic restarts, but they do not want to build or operate the Kubernetes control plane themselves. Which Google Cloud product fits?

choices.text: Cloud Storage, which stores the container images as objects but does not schedule, scale or restart running containers
Compute Engine alone, where the company installs and upgrades Kubernetes itself on its own virtual machines
Looker, which analyzes the performance data of the services but does not run containers
Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), a managed Kubernetes service in which Google operates the control plane and can manage nodes

stem: Two platform teams use GKE. The first employs experienced Kubernetes engineers who must tune node hardware, networking and scheduling for specialized workloads. The second is a small team that wants Google to manage nodes, scaling and security defaults so it can focus on shipping. Which GKE mode statement matches best?

choices.text: Both teams must choose Autopilot, because Standard mode is only for development environments and is not supported for production
The first team prefers Autopilot for configuration control; the second prefers Standard, where Google manages the nodes
Both teams must choose Standard, because Autopilot clusters cannot run production workloads or use Kubernetes features
The first team prefers Standard mode for configuration control; the second prefers Autopilot, where Google manages the nodes

stem: A media company packaged its web application as a container. Traffic is unpredictable: it spikes during live events and drops to nothing overnight. The company wants to pay only while requests are being handled and has no staff to manage servers or clusters. Which product best fits?

choices.text: GKE Standard, where the team sizes, upgrades and monitors node pools to match the changing traffic by itself
Cloud Run, a serverless platform that runs containers, scales with requests including down to zero and charges for use
Cloud Storage, which hosts static files cheaply but does not run an application container
Compute Engine with a fixed number of VMs, which stay running and billed around the clock whatever the traffic

stem: An online photo service wants small pieces of code to run automatically each time a customer uploads a picture, for example to create a thumbnail and record it in a database. The team does not want to run any servers or keep anything idle in between uploads. Which Google Cloud capability fits?

choices.text: Cloud Run functions, triggered by Cloud Storage when a new object is written and billed for execution time
A GKE cluster sized for the busiest hour of the year, with nodes already running to process each uploaded picture
Apigee, which would document and rate-limit the upload API but would not itself create the thumbnail
A permanent Compute Engine VM that polls the bucket for new pictures and keeps running between uploads

stem: A retailer is choosing a home for three workloads. Workload 1 is a legacy package that needs its own operating system. Workload 2 is a set of many containerized microservices that need fine control over networking and scheduling. Workload 3 is a stateless containerized web front end with spiky traffic that the team does not want to operate. Which match is best?

choices.text: Workload 1 on Compute Engine, workload 2 on GKE, workload 3 on Cloud Run
Workload 1 on Cloud Run functions, workload 2 on Cloud Run, workload 3 on Compute Engine
Workload 1 on Cloud Run, workload 2 on Compute Engine, workload 3 on GKE
Workload 1 on GKE, workload 2 on Cloud Run functions, workload 3 on Compute Engine

stem: A product owner is asked to summarize the business value of serverless computing on Google Cloud for the leadership team. Which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The business must size and patch the underlying servers itself, which gives it the most hardware control
Using serverless means the application cannot be connected to databases, storage or other Google Cloud services
Serverless is suitable only for very large always-on workloads, because small variable ones cannot be scaled
Developers deploy code without provisioning or managing servers, so teams can focus on building features
Capacity scales automatically with demand and billing follows use, so idle periods need not cost money

stem: A consultancy holds customer data in Amazon S3 and in Azure Blob Storage. Its analysts know BigQuery and want to query that data with BigQuery SQL from one interface, without copying everything into Google Cloud first. Which product supports this?

choices.text: Cloud Run functions, which would need custom code to copy the data into one bucket before analysis
BigQuery Omni, which runs BigQuery analytics on data stored in Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage
Compute Engine, which hosts virtual machines where analysts would install their own query tools on each cloud
Cloud SQL, a managed relational database that stores data inside its own instances rather than querying external storage

stem: A regulated utility wants a high-performance PostgreSQL-compatible database with Google's enhancements, but regulations require it to run in its own data center, even when disconnected from the internet. Which product fits?

A folder for the retail division that holds the projects, with the policy set at the folder so it flows down to them
A separate billing account for every project, since a billing account carries the security and access rules of the projects that are linked to it
The individual resources inside each project, such as every virtual machine and every storage bucket, configuring the policy on each of them separately

stem: A multinational has hundreds of projects owned by many teams and wants the Google Cloud resource hierarchy to help with governance. Which TWO benefits does the hierarchy provide? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Policies set on a folder are permanently locked once saved and cannot be changed by anyone, including the people who are responsible for them
Every project automatically receives identical built-in spending limits from its parent, so the company never needs to create budgets or quotas
Access control and policies set high in the hierarchy are inherited by the resources below, which keeps security and compliance consistent
Resources in different projects of the organization are blocked from communicating with each other under any circumstances once the hierarchy exists
A single organization-level view lets auditors and administrators see and review the projects, folders and resources in the company

stem: A team configures a budget for its project with alert threshold rules at 50, 90 and 100 percent. After the project passes 100 percent of the budget, the team is surprised that its applications keep running and no services have been shut off. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: A budget with threshold rules is alerts-only: it notifies recipients as spend crosses percentages and does not itself stop resources
Google Cloud ignores budgets for any project that uses more than one service, so the threshold alerts never applied to this project
Threshold rules only start working after an administrator manually approves each alert, so the project was not yet being watched by the budget
The budget was misconfigured, because a budget always disables the whole project and all its services once the final threshold is reached

stem: A startup is worried that a coding mistake, or stolen credentials, could create thousands of virtual machines overnight and produce a very large bill. It wants a built-in safeguard that limits how many resources a project can consume, not just a notification afterwards. Which control fits?

choices.text: A resource quota on the project, which restricts how much of a resource it can use and blocks consumption beyond that
A longer approval workflow in which finance signs every invoice before the payment is made to Google
A larger billing account, since bigger accounts automatically refuse any request for more than the average level of resource use
A weekly Cloud Billing report that the finance manager reads on Monday morning to look for anything unusual in the past week of spending

stem: A media company runs a large video-rendering job every night. The job is split into many independent pieces that can be retried, and the deadline is the next morning, so a few interrupted pieces only cause a delay. The company wants to reduce compute cost. Which approach best balances cost and risk?

choices.text: Run the job on Spot VMs, accepting that capacity may be reclaimed, because the work is fault-tolerant and restartable
Cancel the nightly job and render each video on request when a customer asks for it, accepting longer customer waits
Buy a fleet of standard VMs sized for the nightly peak and leave it running day and night to avoid interruptions
Run the job on Spot VMs and also move the customer payment service, which must stay up around the clock, onto them

stem: An AI research team needs accelerators (GPUs) for a training run that can start whenever capacity becomes available. Capacity for these high-demand resources is scarce, and the finance lead does not want to pay for reserved hardware that sits idle while the team waits. Which Google Cloud approach fits?

choices.text: Ask for a permanent standard reservation of the maximum GPU capacity the team could ever need and keep it for all months of the year
Use the Dynamic Workload Scheduler, which provisions scarce GPUs and TPUs when available, so the team need not hold idle hardware
Run the training on Spot VMs only, since they are the cheapest option
Buy GPUs outright, install them in the company's own server room and depreciate the purchase over several years

stem: A software company runs its application in production. Developers see that the application is slow and want to find which functions and lines of code use the most CPU and memory while real users are on the service. Which Google Cloud Observability tool should they use?

choices.text: Cloud Logging, which stores and searches the text messages written by the application
Cloud Trace, which follows a single request through several services and records its latency
Cloud Profiler, a low-overhead tool that continuously samples running applications by call stack
Error Reporting, which groups application crashes and exceptions by their likely root cause

stem: An online store built from several microservices receives complaints that checkout is slow. No service reports errors and all of them look healthy individually. The operations lead wants to see how long a single customer request spends in each service it passes through, to find the slowest step. Which tool fits best?

choices.text: Cloud Trace, which follows a request across services and shows how much latency each step adds
Error Reporting, because slow checkout is an error that it would group by root cause
A weekly cost report, because slow requests always mean the services were expensive to run
Cloud Profiler, because it shows how much CPU each service uses over the whole week

stem: After a new release, an application throws a mix of exceptions. The development manager wants a view that shows which kinds of errors are happening, how often each occurs and when a new type first appears, rather than reading thousands of raw messages. Which tool provides this?

choices.text: Cloud Profiler, which shows where the code spends its CPU time and memory rather than listing and grouping exceptions
Error Reporting, which aggregates application error events into groups by root cause and lets teams triage them
Cloud Trace, which charts request latency but does not categorize exceptions
Cloud Monitoring uptime checks, which only report whether the website responded to probes sent from various locations

stem: An operations director wants two capabilities: a chart plus an automatic notification to the on-call team whenever the average response time rises above an agreed level, and a searchable record of exactly what each application and the platform did around the time of an incident. Which combination of tools matches these needs?

choices.text: Cloud Profiler for the notification, and Error Reporting for the searchable record of every event and message
Cloud Logging for the chart and the notification, and Cloud Monitoring for the searchable record of events and messages
Cloud Monitoring for the chart and alerting policy, and Cloud Logging for the searchable record of events
Cloud Trace for both, because traces store metrics and event text in the same place

stem: A CIO asks the cloud team to explain what operational excellence means for the company's cloud workloads and what it relies on. Which statement matches Google's description?

choices.text: Keeping every operation manual and approved by a single senior engineer, so that each change is checked by hand
Reaching a state in which no incident ever occurs, after which the monitoring tools can safely be switched off
Buying the most expensive infrastructure available so that no workload ever needs maintenance or monitoring again
Operating workloads efficiently through automation, orchestration and data-driven insights, with continuous learning

stem: A bank states that its payments service must keep working for customers even if one server or one building fails, and that it must also consistently do what customers expect. Which pair of terms describes these two goals?

choices.text: High availability for staying up through a component failure, and reliability for consistently doing its job
Latency for staying up through the failure of a component, and saturation for consistently doing its job
Scalability for staying up through the failure of a component, and quota for consistently doing its job
Reliability for staying up through the failure of a component, and capital expenditure for consistently doing its job

stem: A healthcare provider is designing a patient-records system on Google Cloud that must keep running if a failure affects one location and must not lose records. Which TWO design approaches support this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Turn off monitoring in production to avoid noise, since failures will be reported by users
Replicate data to another location and keep regular backups that can be restored
Size the system for today's load only and add capacity manually when users complain about slowness
Place the application and its only copy of the data on one large server, which is simpler to manage
Run redundant copies of the application in more than one zone, or region, so that another copy can serve users if one fails

stem: A team replicates its customer database to a second region in real time. An employee mistakenly deletes an important table. The manager is surprised that the second region does not hold the table either. What does this show?

choices.text: Backups and replication are exactly the same thing, so adding backups would not have changed the outcome
The replication was set up incorrectly, because a correct replica always keeps old data after a delete
Replication is useful only to reduce running costs, so it was never meant to help in this kind of situation at all
Replication protects against a site failure but copies mistakes too, so backups are also needed to restore deleted data

stem: An operations team uses the four golden signals to monitor a web service: latency, traffic, errors and saturation. During a sales event the team sees that memory use and the request queue are close to the limits of what the service can handle, although response times are still normal. Which signal is this, and what does it warn about?

choices.text: Latency, because it shows how long users must wait for responses and whether they are already slow
Errors, because it counts the requests that have already failed with an error code returned to users
Saturation, because it shows how full the service is and warns of nearing capacity before users are affected
Traffic, because it measures how many requests the service receives each second during the sales event

stem: An online ticket seller wants alerts that reflect what customers actually experience, rather than internal machine statistics. Which TWO of the following best show that customers are being harmed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The number of employees on the on-call rota, because more people on call means fewer customer errors
The total number of log lines produced, because more logs always mean more customers
Rate of errors, because failed requests mean customers cannot complete their purchases
Saturation of the build servers used by developers, because their load decides customers' wait time
Latency of requests, because slow responses frustrate customers even when the service is technically up

stem: A software provider sells a hosted service to business customers. Its engineers track the percentage of successful requests every day. The leadership sets an internal target of 99.95 percent. The contract with customers promises 99.9 percent per month, with service credits if the provider misses it. Which statement maps these three items to SRE terms correctly?

choices.text: The measured success percentage is the SLI, the 99.95 percent target is the SLO and the contract promise with credits is the SLA
The measured success percentage is the SLO, the 99.95 percent target is the SLA and the contract promise with credits is the SLI
The measured success percentage is the SLA, the 99.95 percent target is the SLI and the contract promise with credits is the SLO
All three are SLAs, because each of them is a number related to availability

stem: A home-improvement retailer wants independent software vendors and partner agencies to build apps on top of its product-catalog APIs. Today each partner emails the IT team to learn how the APIs work and to get access credentials, and onboarding takes weeks. Which capability of Apigee API Management addresses this most directly?

choices.text: A container platform that runs every partner's application inside the retailer's own clusters so that the IT team controls the partner code
An API proxy layer that copies the catalog database into each partner's own project so that partners no longer need to call any of the retailer's APIs
A data warehouse that stores all partner questions and answers so that the IT team can reply to each onboarding email more quickly
A developer portal where partners discover the APIs, read the documentation and register their apps themselves without waiting for the IT team

stem: A bank exposes an account-lookup API to partner fintech companies. One partner's faulty script suddenly sends a huge number of requests and slows the bank's backend system for every other partner. The bank wants to protect the backend without changing the backend code. What should it do?

choices.text: Move the backend system to a larger group of virtual machines so that it can absorb any number of requests from any single partner
Apply traffic-management policies such as rate limits and quotas in the Apigee API proxy layer, so that each partner has its own allowance
Ask every partner to promise in writing that it will not send too many requests, and review the contracts again at the end of each year, trusting that no script will ever misbehave
Remove the API from the partner portal so that no partner can use it until all partners have rebuilt their applications

stem: An executive asks why the company should publish public APIs at all. Which TWO statements describe real business benefits of doing so? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A stable API lets the company change or modernize its backend systems while apps and partners keep calling the same interface
Each published API transfers ownership of the data it returns to the partners that call it, outside the company's control
Publishing an API lets the company stop securing and monitoring the systems behind it, since callers reach them via the interface
Public APIs require partners to adopt the company's internal systems and data formats, which merges the two organizations' IT
Partners and developers can build new products on the company's capabilities, which widens its reach and can create revenue through API products

stem: A travel company offers its booking API to many partner websites. The product manager cannot say which partners call the API most, which API versions are still used, or where errors cluster, and therefore cannot decide what to improve or retire. Which Apigee capability answers these questions?

choices.text: A database migration tool, which copies the booking data to a new location so that usage can be counted from the copy
API analytics and monitoring, which show traffic, usage by consumer and error patterns across the company's APIs
A virtual machine image, which captures the server's disk so that engineers can inspect usage on it later
A load balancer, which spreads requests evenly across servers so that every partner receives exactly the same traffic

stem: A film studio renders animated scenes on a render farm that needs specific CPU and memory sizes and GPU accelerators. The studio wants to pick the hardware shape for each job, run licensed rendering software that is installed on a full operating system, and stop paying when a job ends. Which product fits best?

choices.text: Compute Engine, because VMs let the studio choose machine shapes and GPUs, control the operating system, and delete them after use
Cloud Run functions, because small event-driven functions run the rendering software without any operating system or hardware choice to manage
Apigee, because its proxy layer chooses CPU and GPU hardware for each rendering job based on the API calls received
Cloud Storage, because storing the scene files in buckets also performs the rendering calculations without any servers

stem: A retailer's CTO wants to explain what modern application development on Google Cloud gives the business. Which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Microservices can be scaled and updated independently, so a busy checkout service can grow without redeploying the whole application
Keeping the features in one large shared codebase makes each feature faster to release because teams share a single deployment
Moving to the cloud makes an application highly available by itself, so redundancy and monitoring can be left out of the design
Building on containers and managed services makes cost planning unnecessary, because charges stop once the application is deployed
Using managed services lets small teams spend less time on patching and operating infrastructure and more time on features customers see

stem: An online payments company receives a notification call from its card processor each time a payment settles. The call must trigger a few lines of code that update an order status. Settlements arrive unevenly through the day and the company does not want to manage servers or pay for idle capacity. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: A dedicated virtual machine in Compute Engine that runs around the clock so that it is always ready for the next settlement
A new on-premises server that the company buys, installs and patches so that it can keep the code close to its own team
Cloud Run functions, because the small piece of code runs only when a request arrives and the platform handles scaling and servers
A self-managed Kubernetes cluster sized for the busiest hour of the year and left running at that size all year long

stem: A regional bank has agreed to migrate to Google Cloud. Its workloads include a customer-facing mobile backend, a payment core and an internal staff-lunch ordering tool. The steering committee wants to build migration skills and confidence before touching critical systems. Which first step is most sensible?

choices.text: Migrate the low-risk internal lunch-ordering tool as a pilot first, learn from it, and then apply the lessons to more critical workloads
Move all workloads on the same weekend so that the bank never has to run two environments in parallel
Delay the migration until every application has been rewritten as microservices, because nothing should move before that
Start with the payment core, because proving the hardest workload first shows the cloud can handle the bank's most valuable system

stem: A gaming company has players in North America, Europe and Asia. It wants one public entry point for the game's web services that sends each player to the closest healthy set of servers and keeps working if one region has a problem. Which capability supports this goal?

choices.text: A nightly backup of the game's data to cheaper storage, which protects data but does not direct player traffic anywhere
Spot VMs, which are discounted machines that can be stopped by Google and therefore help only with cost, not with traffic routing
Autoscaling a single group of servers in one region, which adds machines when load rises but cannot place servers near each player
Global load balancing, which distributes incoming traffic across backends in several regions and routes around unhealthy ones

stem: An employee opens an email attachment that looks like an invoice. Afterward, the employee's computer runs hidden software that records keystrokes and quietly sends them to an outside party. What is the best name for this kind of threat?

choices.text: Data residency, because the company chose to keep information in a particular geographic location
Malware, because software designed to harm or spy on a system was delivered through an attachment and ran without the user's knowledge
A distributed denial-of-service attack, because many sources flood a service with requests until legitimate users cannot reach it
A misconfiguration, because an administrator set a cloud resource up in a way that left it open to the public

stem: A health insurer wants to protect member data in two situations: when records are copied from its branch offices to Google Cloud over the internet, and when the records sit on disks in the cloud. Which TWO protections address these situations? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Encryption in transit, which scrambles data while it moves across the network so that interceptors cannot read it
A public bucket policy, which lets anyone read the files so that the branch offices can fetch them without credentials
Data deletion every hour, which removes the records so that there is nothing left to protect during the transfer
Encryption in use only, which protects the data while a processor is working on it but not while it moves or sits on disk
Encryption at rest, which scrambles stored data so that someone who obtains the disks or files cannot read the contents

stem: A retailer passes its annual compliance audit. Three months later attackers steal customer data through an old, unpatched system that the audit checklist did not cover. A director asks whether passing the audit meant the company was secure. What is the best answer?

choices.text: Not necessarily: compliance shows required controls were met at one point in time, while security is ongoing defense against real threats
No, because a successful theft shows that the audit was carried out incorrectly and that its passing result should be withdrawn
Yes, because a compliance certificate shows that the company's security controls are sufficient to stop attacks on its systems
Yes, because auditors keep watching the company's systems between audits and would have flagged the old system before the theft

stem: A hospital reviews three incidents. In the first, a lost laptop exposed patient names. In the second, an error silently altered medication doses in a database. In the third, a ransomware attack made the scheduling system unusable for a day. Which mapping to confidentiality, integrity and availability is correct?

choices.text: All three are confidentiality, because every incident involved patient information being at risk in some way
Lost laptop is integrity, altered doses are availability, and the unusable scheduling system is confidentiality
Lost laptop is confidentiality, altered doses are integrity, and the unusable scheduling system is availability
Lost laptop is availability, altered doses are confidentiality, and the unusable scheduling system is integrity

stem: A contractor signs in to the company's cloud environment with a password and a phone code. When the contractor tries to open the payroll data, access is refused. Later, auditors review a record showing who attempted to open it. Which description matches the three terms?

choices.text: Authentication is the refusal of payroll access, auditing is the sign-in itself, and authorization is the record auditors review later, created only if the contractor were let in
Auditing is the sign-in, authorization is the password and phone code, and authentication is the refusal of payroll access
Authorization is the sign-in, authentication is the refusal of payroll access, and auditing is the password and phone code
Authentication is the sign-in that proves identity, authorization is the refusal for lack of permission, and auditing is the record of who tried

stem: A software company runs a three-tier application in Google Cloud: web servers, application servers and databases. Its security team wants traffic between tiers to be allowed only where the application needs it, using centrally managed rules that can be applied consistently to many resources. Which Google Cloud capability fits?

choices.text: Spot VMs, which lower the cost of fault-tolerant machines but do not decide which connections are permitted
Looker dashboards, which show charts of the traffic between tiers but cannot allow or block any of it
Cloud Storage storage classes, which move rarely used objects to cheaper storage and never decide which network connections are permitted
Cloud NGFW firewall policies, which define allow and deny rules for network traffic and apply them consistently across resources

stem: After a sensitive dataset was changed, the security lead asks: who made the change, on which resource and at what time? The company wants Google Cloud to answer such "who did what, where and when" questions for investigations and audits. Which capability provides this?

choices.text: Apigee analytics, which report how partner applications use published APIs but not who changed cloud resources
Cloud Audit Logs in Cloud Logging, which record administrative activities and resource access across Google Cloud services
A load balancer, which spreads user traffic across servers but does not keep a record of administrative actions
Cloud Storage Archive class, which keeps rarely read data at low cost for long periods but does not record who changed resources

stem: A company hosts its development, testing and production applications in Google Cloud. Security wants the networks of these environments to be logically separated, with private IP addressing and control over what can connect to what. Which Google Cloud service provides these networking building blocks?

choices.text: Dynamic Workload Scheduler, which obtains GPU and TPU capacity for batch and training jobs
Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), a global software-defined network with subnets and firewall rules
Looker, which presents business intelligence dashboards built on governed semantic data models
Cloud Run functions, which run small pieces of event-driven code that scale with incoming requests

stem: A regulated customer asks how Google protects the servers themselves before any customer workload runs on them, because attackers can target the boot process and hardware supply chain. Which statement reflects Google's approach?

choices.text: Google relies only on perimeter firewalls, so the servers themselves are not specially protected from tampering
Google disables all logging on the servers so that attackers cannot find out anything about the infrastructure
Google designs its own server boards and network gear, vets component vendors, and uses secure boot so servers start only the intended software
Google rents ordinary servers from outside vendors and leaves it to each customer to check the boot software on them, with no controls of its own over the hardware supply chain

stem: A software company runs a customer database and application servers that need to stay on for at least the next three years at a steady, predictable level. The finance team wants to lower the unit cost of this baseline capacity and is willing to plan ahead. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Committed use discounts, in which the company agrees to a defined amount of resource use for a period in exchange for a lower cost
Moving the data to Archive storage, because rarely accessed storage is the cheapest place for a live database
Cancelling all quotas, so that the servers can grow without limit and the finance team never needs to plan capacity
Spot VMs for the database, because Google may stop them at any time, which is acceptable for a steady customer-facing database

stem: A company shares one Google Cloud billing account among marketing, logistics and research. Finance wants to charge each department for its own cloud use and analyze spend with SQL and dashboards. Which approach supports this best?

choices.text: Give each department a separate credit card so that the cloud provider sends them independent bills with no shared data
Organize resources into projects and labels per department, and export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery to allocate cost by department
Stop using cloud services and return to buying servers, because shared costs cannot be assigned to departments in the cloud and on-premises costs never need to be shared
Use one project for everything and ask departments to estimate their use by hand at the end of the year

stem: A company wants to lower its cloud spend without hurting customers. Which TWO actions are cost-saving practices that fit their intended use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Run the customer-facing payment database on Spot VMs, since customers rarely mind when the service pauses suddenly
Disable budgets and alerts so that teams are not distracted by spending notices during the quarter
Run fault-tolerant, restartable batch jobs on Spot VMs, accepting that Google may stop machines in exchange for lower cost
Keep all development environments running at full size around the clock so that nobody has to restart them
Use autoscaling so that the number of servers follows demand instead of staying sized for the busiest day

stem: A service promises 99.9 percent of successful requests in a month as its internal target (SLO). By mid-month it has used little of the allowed failures. The product manager wants to know how to use the remaining allowance. What does the error budget suggest?

choices.text: The error budget is the penalty the customer receives from Google Cloud when the SLO is missed in any month
The error budget is a financial limit on cloud spending, so the team must stop using the service when it is reached
The remaining error budget shows that monitoring can be turned off for the rest of the month, since failures are now permitted and nobody needs to look at dashboards any more
Remaining budget leaves room for reasonable risk, such as faster releases, while a nearly spent budget calls for focusing on reliability

stem: A company runs applications in dozens of projects. When something goes wrong, engineers log in to individual machines and search for text files, and they cannot see what happened across services. Leaders want one place to collect, search and analyze logs from all applications. Which product provides this?

choices.text: Apigee, which manages and secures APIs but does not collect logs from every application in the company
Compute Engine, which provides virtual machines and therefore depends on engineers reading files on each machine
Cloud Storage Coldline class, which stores rarely accessed objects cheaply and cannot be searched by an engineer who needs to follow one request across applications
Cloud Logging, part of Google Cloud Observability, which collects logs from applications and services for central search and analysis

stem: A major outage hits a retailer's checkout. Service is restored, and the CEO asks the SRE lead what should happen next to keep it from happening again. Which practice does Google recommend?

choices.text: Identify the engineer who made the last change and remove that person from the on-call rotation as a deterrent, and warn the rest of the team that mistakes will be punished
Close the incident quietly, because discussing outages with other teams only damages the company's reputation
Hold a post-incident review that documents the timeline, root cause and lessons learned, then act on the recommended improvements
Wait for the next outage and compare it with this one, since a single event cannot show anything useful

stem: A payments company runs its customer portal in one Google Cloud region, spread across several zones. The board now asks for protection against the unlikely event that an entire region becomes unavailable, for example because of a regional disaster. Which approach addresses this requirement?

choices.text: Move the portal's static images to edge locations, so that pages load faster for distant customers
Deploy the portal in two or more regions, so that traffic can be served from another region if one is lost
Add more virtual machines to the existing zones, so that each zone has extra capacity during busy periods
Increase the network bandwidth of the current region, so that more requests can be served each second

stem: A food manufacturer wants real-time quality checks on its factory floor, where a delay of even a second would stop a production line, and its plants have unreliable links to the internet. It also wants to analyze the combined data from all plants in the public cloud and migrate other systems gradually. Which model fits?

choices.text: Hybrid cloud, with time-critical systems staying at the plants and analytics and other workloads running in the public cloud
Public cloud only, because all workloads should run in the provider's regions, including the machines next to the production line
A single private cloud in one data center, because analytics at scale cannot use any service from a public provider
Multicloud with two public providers, because the plants need a second provider rather than any equipment on site

stem: A global retailer decides to use more than one public cloud provider. Which TWO benefits can the retailer reasonably expect from this multicloud approach? (Select TWO)

choices.text: All provider services connect to each other without any design, so data moves freely at no extra effort
Operations become simpler automatically, because every provider uses identical tools, interfaces and security settings
The retailer no longer needs to manage identity, security or cost across its environments
Less dependence on a single vendor, which improves negotiating power and reduces lock-in risk
Each workload can run on the provider whose services best fit it, such as one provider's analytics with another's application platform

stem: A company currently rents virtual machines, installing and patching the operating system and middleware itself. It is considering moving its custom order application to a platform where developers only deploy code. What changes in who does the work?

choices.text: The provider takes over the operating system, runtime and scaling, and the company concentrates on its code and data
The company gives up control of its application code, because platform services require the provider's developers to maintain it
The company still patches the operating system, but the provider now writes the order application code
The company must buy and operate its own servers again, because platforms run only in private data centers

stem: A film studio must send raw footage of several terabytes to a cloud storage service every night. The editor complains that the upload does not finish before morning, although a single small test file arrives almost instantly. Which networking concept is the studio most likely short of?

choices.text: IP address space, meaning the studio has too few addresses to start more than one upload
Bandwidth, meaning the studio's connection cannot carry enough data per second for such large transfers
Latency, meaning the studio's network has too long a delay before the first byte of a small file arrives
DNS, meaning the storage service's name cannot be translated into the correct numeric address

stem: A 200-person law firm wants a ready-made case-management application that its staff can use next week. The firm has no developers and wants no responsibility for servers. The partners ask what they give up by choosing SaaS rather than building their own application. What is the most accurate answer?

choices.text: They own every feature decision, because the provider only supplies computers and cannot influence the software
They must patch the operating system and database themselves, which makes SaaS slower to start than a custom build
They get less control over features and underlying configuration, in exchange for speed and no infrastructure to manage
They give up the ability to use the application from the internet, because SaaS runs only on the office network

stem: A cosmetics company wants to test five new online campaign ideas in one month, keeping only the ones that attract customers. In its data center, every experiment needs servers that take weeks to order, so the team tests one idea per quarter. Which cloud benefit most directly changes this?

choices.text: Agility, because resources can be created in minutes and released when an experiment ends
Standardization, because every experiment must use the same hardware as the previous one
Compliance, because cloud providers automatically certify every campaign under the company's name
Physical security, because the company's own data center would need guards for each experiment

stem: A manufacturer's board has approved a cloud program, but the CIO warns of two challenges that often derail digital transformation. Which TWO are such challenges? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Legacy applications and siloed data can be hard to move, integrate or modernize
Pay-as-you-go pricing lets teams start small and grow their spending in line with actual usage
A global network lets the company reach customers in new regions with lower latency than before
Managed services take routine patching and hardware upkeep off the internal IT team's workload
Employees may lack new skills and resist changing working habits, which slows adoption

stem: A regional bank notes that customers now expect to open accounts, track payments and resolve problems through an app at any hour, comparing it with the best digital experiences they have had elsewhere. The bank's leaders ask how to describe this force to the board. Which description fits?

choices.text: A regulatory requirement, because laws require every bank to launch a mobile application
A cost-saving initiative, because digital channels reduce the number of branch employees the bank must hire
A technology limitation, because mobile phones cannot yet support secure banking features
A customer-expectation driver of digital transformation, pushing the bank to modernize how it serves people

stem: An online ticket seller expects demand to be small on most days but to jump tenfold when a popular concert goes on sale, then fall again within hours. Leaders want capacity to follow demand in both directions without staff action. Which cloud characteristic is this, and why does it matter?

choices.text: Fixed capacity, which guarantees the same performance by always running the largest possible environment
Elasticity, which adds resources when demand rises and removes them when it falls, so spending follows usage
Data residency, which keeps the sales records in one country to meet local rules
Portability, which lets the seller copy the application to another provider within a few minutes

stem: A company has different departments that each calculate "monthly revenue" in their own spreadsheets, so leaders see different numbers in every meeting. The company wants all dashboards, whatever tool or team produces them, to use one governed definition of each business metric on top of its data warehouse. Which Google Cloud product fits?

choices.text: Looker, because it provides a governed semantic layer where metrics are defined once and reused
Pub/Sub, because it delivers revenue events to the departments' own systems as soon as they happen
Cloud Storage, because it can hold a copy of each department's spreadsheet together in one shared bucket
Cloud Run, because it can host a web application in which the departments type in their own monthly figures

stem: A wind-turbine operator wants to avoid costly failures. Each turbine sends vibration readings every second. Today engineers review a weekly report and find problems after a turbine has already broken. What is the main business value of moving to streaming analytics?

The operator can stop collecting vibration data, since streaming analytics predicts failures without inputs

stem: A marketing director defends the plan to give store managers and marketers self-service BI tools instead of routing every question to the central analytics team. Which TWO benefits can she cite? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Decisions are based on shared, current data, which reduces reliance on instinct and stale spreadsheets
Every user automatically sees all data in the company, including data they are not meant to see
Data governance becomes unnecessary, because dashboards check the accuracy of data automatically
The central analytics team can be dissolved, because nobody needs advanced analysis any more
Business users can answer many questions themselves, which shortens the wait from days to minutes

stem: An online retailer's checkout service receives a huge surge of order events during a flash sale. The order-processing and analytics systems cannot always keep pace, and the company does not want the checkout to slow down or lose orders.
