choices.text: Looker, a BI platform that displays orders on dashboards after they are stored
Cloud Storage, an object store that returns each order to the checkout for processing

stem: A manufacturer's finance application was built for Microsoft SQL Server and the vendor does not support other engines. The manufacturer wants to stop patching database servers and handling backups, but cannot change the application. Which Google Cloud service fits?

choices.text: Bigtable, because it is a wide-column NoSQL database for key-based access
Firestore, because it is a document database for mobile and web applications

stem: A pharmaceutical company wants to collect lab instrument files, scanned reports, images and CSV exports from many research sites in one low-cost place before deciding how to analyze them. Researchers will later load selected data into an analytics engine. Which approach fits this stage?

choices.text: Use Bigtable to keep each scan as a row, because it is built for scanned documents
Keep files in Cloud Storage as the raw lake landing zone and load selected data into BigQuery later
Discard unstructured files, and keep only CSV exports, because analytics cannot use other formats
Load every file into a Cloud SQL table first, so that images and scans become rows and columns

stem: A retailer runs its order system on a Cloud SQL database. Every month-end, analysts run very large reports on the same database, and during these hours customers see slow checkouts. The company wants to keep orders fast and still allow heavy reporting. What is the best approach?

Ask the analysts to run reports more often, so that each run has less data to read
Stop all reporting at month-end, because relational databases cannot support analytics

stem: A telecom company wants to understand its customer data. Which TWO of the following are examples of unstructured data? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A spreadsheet of device serial numbers listed in labeled columns
A table of monthly invoices with fixed columns for customer ID, date and amount
Photographs that technicians take of damaged network equipment
A relational table of plan prices and contract lengths
Recorded audio of customer-service calls

stem: A retailer has customer data in several systems. When a customer changes an address, nobody knows who must correct the other copies, and error reports are passed between departments for months. Give every employee write access to every system, so anyone can fix any record immediately
Move all data into one larger spreadsheet that people on every team can edit at once

stem: A bank's developers have built an AI agent prototype that answers customer questions and calls internal systems. choices.text: Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, a managed environment to deploy and scale agents

Looker, because it is a BI tool that can show charts of agent conversations

stem: A research institute trains very large AI models and worries about slow training, inflexible hardware and rising costs. A consultant describes Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer. Which TWO statements about it are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: It supports only a single type of chip, so every customer must use the same hardware

stem: A law firm's partners spend hours reading long supplier contracts to find key obligations and draft short summaries for clients. choices.text: Cloud Vision API, which detects labels and extracts printed text from scanned contract pages
A custom AutoML image classification model trained on photographs of paper contracts

BigQuery ML linear regression trained on past contract values to predict the value of new ones

stem: A newspaper wants every article to be available as spoken audio, so that readers with visual impairments and commuters can listen. The paper has no AI specialists and wants natural-sounding voices in several languages soon. Which Google Cloud capability fits?

choices.text: Text-to-Speech, a pre-trained API that turns written text into spoken audio
Cloud Vision API, because it reads printed text from images of newspaper pages

stem: An energy retailer deployed a custom model that predicts customer churn. For six months it worked well, but its accuracy has fallen as customer behavior and tariffs changed. choices.text: Use Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform MLOps tools to track drift, retrain on newer data and redeploy

stem: An online marketplace wants to decide which problem to tackle first with machine learning. Which of the following is best suited to ML rather than to a simple fixed rule or ordinary software?

choices.text: Displaying the company logo at the top of every web page

Calculating sales tax for every order from a published rate table of fixed percentages

stem: An insurer plans to let an AI agent handle claims end to end. A compliance officer worries about large claims and unusual cases. Which practice best balances efficiency with accountability?

Automate routine claims, and route large or unusual ones to people for review, with decisions logged

stem: A retail executive looks at a dashboard showing that sales in one region fell sharply last month. Her analyst then examines the data by product, store and promotion to find out why sales fell. Which type of data analytics is the analyst performing?

choices.text: Predictive analytics, which forecasts next quarter's sales using a trained model
Descriptive analytics, which only summarizes what happened without looking at causes

Prescriptive analytics, which automatically changes store prices without human involvement

stem: A company's staff use a generative AI tool to draft customer replies. One reply confidently described a refund policy that does not exist. Leaders want to keep using the tool. Which action best addresses this business risk?

Withdraw the tool from customer replies and go back to staff writing each reply by hand

stem: A humanitarian nonprofit must launch a registration app for displaced families within days after each disaster, in whichever country is affected. choices.text: Guaranteed lower total cost than any on-premises option, because cloud providers price every single workload below the cost of owned hardware
Automatic legal compliance in every country, because a cloud provider takes over the nonprofit's data protection obligations
Speed and agility, because resources can be provisioned in minutes in a suitable region instead of ordering and installing hardware

stem: A distribution company runs its warehouse system on the same number of servers 24 hours a day, every day, with almost no change in load. Which statement about cost-effectiveness is the MOST accurate guidance for this workload?

choices.text: Savings will come automatically from elasticity, because cloud providers scale every steady workload down at night without any planning effort
Savings are impossible for steady workloads, so the company should keep this system on premises and move only its seasonal applications

stem: A three-person fintech startup must show investors and a partner bank that customer data in its new cloud application is protected. Each customer receives a dedicated physical data center, so the startup's hardware is isolated from every other Google Cloud customer
Customer content stored in Google Cloud is encrypted at rest by default, on infrastructure that Google designs, hardens and monitors
Every application deployed on Google Cloud is automatically certified as compliant with the partner bank's own audit requirements

stem: A 90-year-old insurer wants to transform how it serves customers. Buy a ready-made software package for every business process, so that the company no longer needs its own data or its own IT staff

stem: A national tax agency runs its own private cloud for citizen records, which law requires to stay in agency data centers. Use a hybrid cloud that keeps records in the private cloud and adds public cloud capacity for the portal's web tier during the peak
Buy enough private-cloud servers for the spring peak, and lend the spare capacity to other agencies during the remaining months
Move all records and the filing portal to one public cloud region, so the agency stops operating its own data centers

stem: An Australian online pharmacy must keep all customer prescriptions stored in Australia under national health privacy rules. Its checkout must keep working if a single data center area fails, but the board has accepted that a rare outage of a whole region may interrupt sales for a while. Leadership wants the SIMPLEST deployment that satisfies both stated requirements. Which deployment fits BEST?

Deploy in one Australian region plus a second region in Asia, so that a full regional outage never affects checkout
Deploy in one zone of an Asian region close to Australia, and copy nightly backups of prescriptions into Australia
Deploy in a single zone of an Australian region and rely on edge locations worldwide to keep checkout available

stem: A packaging manufacturer moves a 15-year-old quality-control application whose vendor requires a specific operating system version and a licensed agent installed on the server. The manufacturer wants to stop buying and maintaining hardware, but its IT team must keep full control of the operating system and installed software. Which service model gives the needed control with the LEAST loss of flexibility?

Software as a service, because the provider runs the whole application and the manufacturer only manages user accounts and its own data
Platform as a service, because the provider manages the operating system while the team deploys only its application code to the runtime

stem: A sportswear brand keeps its sales history as files in Cloud Storage. The analytics team queries it with BigQuery, while the data science team uses Apache Spark. Today each team keeps its own copy, and the copies disagree. Leadership wants one copy of the data, readable by both teams' engines, with the LEAST risk of being tied to a single vendor's format. Which approach fits BEST?

Keep one copy in an open table format such as Apache Iceberg in Cloud Storage, and expose it to both engines through BigLake tables

Move the files into a spreadsheet that both teams share, so that every analyst and data scientist edits the same document

stem: An online home-goods retailer's ad targeting relied on audience lists bought from data brokers, but browsers now limit cross-site tracking and regulators require clear customer consent for any personal data used in marketing. choices.text: Contextual targeting only, placing ads beside related content without using any information about the retailer's own shoppers

First-party data such as purchases, loyalty activity and site behavior that customers share directly with the retailer under consent
Third-party data, by buying larger audience lists from more brokers so that each campaign reaches more people than before

stem: A law firm must keep signed case files in Cloud Storage for ten years after each case closes. Files are almost never opened again; fewer than one in a thousand is requested in a typical year. When a court does request one, a paralegal must download it within minutes. The firm wants the LOWEST storage cost that still meets this retrieval need. Which storage class fits BEST?

choices.text: Archive storage, because it has the lowest storage cost and still returns data within milliseconds rather than hours
Nearline storage, because files that are read about once a month are the cheapest class that can be downloaded quickly
Coldline storage, because Archive storage keeps data offline and needs several hours to restore before it can be read
Standard storage, because only the class for frequently accessed data can return a file within minutes of a request

stem: A media company is planning three new data stores. Store 1 holds billions of listening events per day and must answer single-key lookups for a user's recent history in milliseconds. Store 2 is a mobile app's user content that must sync in real time and work offline. Store 3 is a booking ledger written from several continents that needs strong consistency everywhere. choices.text: Store 3 on Bigtable, a key-value store that provides multi-table relational transactions with SQL joins

Use business intelligence for both requests, because a dashboard of past rides directly shows tomorrow's exact demand per station

stem: A ticketing company runs a nightly job that reconciles the day's payments: it starts, processes all records and stops, usually within an hour, and it does not answer any web requests. stem: A pharmacy chain lets about forty partner apps call its prescription-status API, and new partners join every month. stem: A retailer moves two workloads to Google Cloud. Its inventory application moves to Compute Engine virtual machines, and its new storefront is deployed as a container on Cloud Run. stem: An audit at a logistics firm finds that 40 developers hold broad administrator roles on every production project "to save time", and that nobody reviews who used those powers. stem: A software company passed its annual compliance audit in January. In June, a security researcher finds that a developer had made a storage bucket public in March, exposing test copies of customer records. stem: An e-commerce company has three security needs. Its public storefront receives SQL injection attempts and traffic floods during sales. Employees must reach internal web tools from home without a traditional VPN. Auditors want to know which storage buckets and tables contain card numbers. The company prefers Google Cloud managed services. Which THREE offerings match these needs? (Select THREE)

choices.text: Cloud VPN, which encrypts traffic between office networks and also blocks SQL injection attempts against the public storefront
Cloud Armor, which filters web attacks such as SQL injection and helps absorb DDoS traffic in front of the storefront
Security Command Center, which replaces the storefront's login page and checks each shopper's password strength
Certificate Manager, which scans BigQuery tables for card numbers and removes the ones that auditors flag as risky
Sensitive Data Protection, which discovers and classifies sensitive data such as card numbers in storage and tables
Identity-Aware Proxy, which lets employees reach internal web apps based on identity and context without a VPN

stem: A European health-data processor must keep patient workloads in EU regions and must limit which Google personnel can access its data, as required by its national regulator. Its small compliance team wants these controls set up as a ready-made package aligned with the regulation, rather than designing and maintaining every policy itself. Which offering fits BEST?

choices.text: Assured Workloads, which creates a controlled environment with data residency, access and personnel controls for regulated workloads
Cloud Interconnect, which gives the processor a dedicated connection and therefore restricts which Google employees see its data
Cloud Monitoring, which shows dashboards of resource usage in each region and sends alerts whenever patient data is read by Google staff
Cloud Armor, which blocks requests from outside Europe and therefore keeps all stored patient data within EU regions

stem: A security operations team collects logs from its cloud projects, on-premises firewalls and employee laptops, and analysts switch between separate tools for searching, case management and response. Investigations often need data from many months back. Leadership wants one platform that keeps this telemetry, correlates it with threat intelligence and automates response steps. Which offering fits BEST?

choices.text: Security Command Center, which manages cloud resource risks and is the main place to keep months of on-premises firewall and laptop logs
Sensitive Data Protection, which correlates firewall alerts with threat intelligence and opens investigation cases automatically
Cloud Armor, which collects endpoint and firewall logs from every office and runs automated response playbooks for analysts
Google Security Operations, which ingests and retains security telemetry, detects threats and supports investigation and response

stem: A university gives each student team a Google Cloud project for a hackathon. The teams deploy their apps on Cloud Run. The department fears a runaway loop could create a large bill, and it wants usage on a project to be paused automatically when the project's budget is reached, not just reported. Which control fits BEST?

choices.text: An alerts-only budget with email notifications, because a budget alert stops Cloud Run as soon as the threshold is crossed
Committed use discounts for each project, because a commitment fixes the maximum amount that the project can ever spend
A spend cap budget on each project for Cloud Run, which pauses that service's usage when the budget amount is reached
A monthly billing report reviewed by the department, so that staff can delete expensive projects at the end of each month

stem: A European bank organizes its Google Cloud projects in folders by business unit. A new regulation says no resource of the retail unit may be created outside EU locations, including in projects that will be created next year. The cloud team wants to enforce this centrally, with the LEAST per-project work. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: An organization policy that restricts resource locations, set on the retail folder so that current and future projects inherit it
A predefined IAM role granted on each retail project separately, which removes the permission to create resources outside EU locations
A budget alert on each retail project that emails the security team whenever spend appears in a region outside the EU
A written guideline sent to every retail developer, asking them to choose EU locations whenever they create new resources

stem: A media group has more than 300 projects owned by many teams. Finance suspects that idle virtual machines and oversized machines waste money, but no one has time to review every project by hand, and team leads dispute estimates that are not based on real usage. The CFO wants a data-driven list of savings opportunities with the LEAST manual analysis. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Ask each team to estimate its own waste in a spreadsheet each quarter, and add up the estimates for the CFO
Use Active Assist recommendations, which analyze usage and suggest actions such as removing idle VMs and resizing machines
Move every project to Spot VMs, so that Google reclaims idle machines automatically whenever they are not used
Buy committed use discounts for all current virtual machines, so that the idle machines become cheaper to keep running all year

stem: A payroll software provider tracks the share of successful payroll runs each month. Engineering wants an internal goal of 99.9 percent, while the contract with customers promises 99.5 percent with service credits if missed. The product director asks the team to label each part correctly for the operations handbook. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The share of successful runs is the SLA, because measurements become agreements once they are reported
The internal 99.9 percent goal is the service level agreement (SLA), because engineering signs it off
The 99.5 percent contract promise is the SLO, because any target that customers can see is by definition an objective
The internal 99.9 percent goal is the service level objective (SLO), the target the team aims to meet
The share of successful payroll runs is the service level indicator (SLI), the measurement of service behavior

stem: A ride-hailing company's matching service must keep working if one zone fails and must recover within minutes if an entire region becomes unavailable. Completed trips are the basis for driver payments, so losing even a few seconds of trip records is unacceptable to finance. The operations team is small and cannot run manual recovery steps at night. Which design addresses all of these requirements BEST?

choices.text: Redundant instances across zones plus synchronous replication of trip data to another region with automated failover
A content delivery network in front of the service, so that cached pages keep riders matched with drivers during any outage
Nightly backups to a storage bucket in the same zone, restored manually to a new region after any outage
A single large server with redundant power supplies, placed in the zone with the best historical uptime

stem: A regional hospital network fears ransomware after a nearby hospital was locked out of its systems for two weeks. Its board has decided never to pay a ransom, and clinical systems must be restored within one day after any attack. The CISO must choose controls that reduce both the chance of infection and the business impact of a successful attack. Which TWO measures fit BEST? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Store the only copy of each backup on the same servers as the clinical systems, so restores are as fast as possible
Require multi-factor authentication and least-privilege access, so stolen passwords alone cannot spread the attack widely
Rely on paying a negotiated ransom as the recovery plan, because decryption keys always restore every system within a day
Turn off all logging during normal operation, so that attackers cannot read log files to learn about the hospital's systems
Keep backups isolated from the production environment and protected from deletion, and test restoring them regularly

stem: An engineering consultancy is moving three systems out of its server room. Its timesheet and expense process should use an off-the-shelf application because the firm has no developers for it. Its own project-pricing engine is custom code that developers update weekly, and they want to stop managing operating systems. Its structural-analysis package is licensed software whose installation guide requires a specific operating system release and a kernel driver on the machine. Leadership wants each system on the service model that removes the most operational work without breaking a requirement. Which assignment is BEST?

choices.text: Timesheets on IaaS virtual machines, pricing engine on SaaS, structural-analysis package on PaaS with a managed runtime
Timesheets on PaaS with custom code, pricing engine on serverless functions, structural-analysis package on a SaaS subscription
Timesheets on SaaS, pricing engine on PaaS or serverless, structural-analysis package on IaaS virtual machines
Timesheets on SaaS, pricing engine on IaaS virtual machines, structural-analysis package on a serverless container platform

stem: A European payments company is adopting Google Cloud. Its financial regulator requires a documented, tested exit plan showing that critical workloads could move to another provider within a reasonable period. The company's platform team of six wants managed services rather than running infrastructure itself. While reviewing current tools, the architect notes that the data science team runs Apache Spark notebooks against the same transaction history that finance analysts will query in BigQuery, and both teams must work from one copy. Which strategy satisfies all three requirements BEST?

choices.text: Run every application in two public clouds at full capacity at all times, copying the transaction history to each cloud every hour
Use only proprietary serverless services for applications and data, and write the exit plan as a full rewrite on the other provider
Run every workload on self-managed virtual machines with open-source software installed by the team, avoiding all managed services
Run applications as containers on GKE and keep transaction history in an open table format queried through BigLake tables

stem: A design-software company serves all customers from one Google Cloud region in the United States. Customers in Japan now make up a third of revenue and complain that each click in the editor feels slow. The office manager proposes buying a faster internet line for the Tokyo sales office. Measurements show each request is small, but the round trip from Japan to the region takes far longer than from US cities. The engineers add that editor clicks call an API whose responses are personalized and cannot be cached. Customer data may legally be stored in either country. Which action addresses the root cause BEST?

choices.text: Deploy the API tier and the data it reads in a Google Cloud region in Japan, so requests travel a much shorter distance
Increase the machine size of the US servers, so that each API request is processed faster once it reaches the region
Put a content delivery network in front of the US region, so that edge locations in Japan answer the editor's API calls
Upgrade the Tokyo office's internet line to a much higher bandwidth, so that each editor request transfers to the region faster

stem: A concert-ticket marketplace sells seats for the same events to buyers in North America, Europe and Asia at the same moment when sales open. Its developers write relational SQL and want transactions across seats, orders and payments. The business requires the service to accept purchases in every region even during a regional outage, with the highest availability Google Cloud offers. A post-mortem from last year adds that two buyers on different continents were both sold the final seat of a show, which the company must never repeat. Which database fits BEST?

choices.text: Bigtable with clusters replicated across three continents, so each region writes seats locally with low latency
Spanner in a multi-region configuration, giving relational transactions with strong consistency across regions
Cloud SQL with read replicas in other regions, so buyers on each continent read seat maps from a nearby copy
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL in one region with a columnar engine, so seat queries and purchase transactions run fast

stem: A market-research firm stores two kinds of files in Cloud Storage and wants the LOWEST total cost for each. Raw survey uploads are read about once a month by analysts and are deleted 60 days after upload under the firm's privacy policy. Signed client reports must be kept for three years; auditors read every report twice a year. The finance lead reminds the team that a class's minimum storage duration is charged even when an object is deleted earlier. Which TWO choices are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Raw survey uploads in Coldline storage, because its lower at-rest price outweighs a 90-day minimum on 60-day files
Raw survey uploads in Archive storage, because deleting the files early avoids paying for its 365-day minimum storage duration
Raw survey uploads in Nearline storage, because monthly reads fit it and the 60-day life exceeds its 30-day minimum
Signed client reports in Archive storage, because any data kept longer than one year belongs in the coldest class
Signed client reports in Coldline storage, because reads twice a year fit at most once a quarter over three years

stem: A utilities company is building a mobile app for about 800 field inspectors who record pole and transformer inspections on company phones. The inspection forms change often as regulators add questions, so the data structure must be flexible. The company has no database administrators and wants a fully managed, serverless database. The project brief also notes that many inspections happen in rural valleys with no mobile signal, and supervisors want to see completed inspections the moment a device reconnects. Which database fits BEST?

choices.text: Bigtable, because a wide-column store handles flexible fields and synchronizes each inspector's phone while it is offline
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, because relational tables with a fixed schema keep frequently changing inspection forms consistent everywhere
Spanner, because global strong consistency lets inspectors write records in valleys where phones have no connection at all
Firestore, a serverless document database with flexible documents, offline support and real-time sync on reconnection

stem: An online grocer wants a live view of orders by store. Order events already flow into Pub/Sub. Before analysis, each event must be deduplicated, enriched with the store's region and aggregated per minute, and analysts will query the results in BigQuery. The data team also runs about fifty existing Apache Spark batch jobs on an on-premises cluster whose hardware support ends in two months, and the team cannot rewrite them before then. Which plan meets these requirements with the LEAST rework?

choices.text: Write orders directly to BigQuery with a BigQuery subscription, and rewrite the Spark jobs as SQL in BigQuery within two months
Process orders with Dataflow from Pub/Sub into BigQuery, and move the Spark jobs to Managed Service for Apache Spark
Send each order to a Cloud Run function that writes into Cloud SQL, and rewrite the Spark jobs as Dataflow pipelines now
Process orders with Spark Streaming on new self-managed virtual machines, and keep the batch jobs on the old cluster longer

stem: A home-appliance maker has three AI requests and a small analytics team. First, customer reviews arrive in eleven languages, and the quality team wants them all in English this month. Second, SQL analysts want to predict which registered appliances will need a repair visit; the data is in BigQuery and policy forbids exporting customer records. Third, the factory wants cameras to classify its own patented hinge defects, for which inspectors have labeled thousands of photos; general image labels do not cover these defects. Which THREE choices fit BEST? (Select THREE)

choices.text: Export customer records to a separate training cluster for the repair model, and have a new Python team build it from scratch
Use the pre-trained Vision API for the hinge defects, because its general labels already recognize patented hinge failures
Use BigQuery ML for the repair prediction, so analysts build the model in SQL where the customer data already sits
Use AutoML to build a custom translation model for the reviews, training it from scratch on the company's past documents first
Use the pre-trained Translation API for the reviews, because translation needs no model training and can start this month
Use AutoML on Agent Platform for the hinge defects, training a custom image model from the inspectors' labeled photos

stem: A biotech research group must fine-tune a language model on 16 GPUs for about four days. GPUs of that type are often scarce in its preferred region. The run can start any time in the next two weeks, the group will do this only twice this year, and its grant cannot fund long-term commitments. The group's lead engineer notes that the training code has no checkpointing yet, so if any machine is interrupted the whole run must start again from the beginning. Which way of obtaining the GPUs fits BEST?

choices.text: Standard on-demand VMs requested at a random time, hoping that all 16 GPUs are free in the zone whenever the team asks for them
Spot VMs, because their large discounts suit a tight grant and the run can simply be repeated after any preemption
A three-year resource-based committed use discount on 16 GPUs, because it gives the deepest discount for these machines
Flex-start VMs through Dynamic Workload Scheduler, which wait for scarce capacity and then run without preemption for a bounded time

stem: A national clinic network built a model to predict which patients will miss appointments, so staff can send reminders. It was trained on two years of data from city clinics and reached high overall accuracy. After a nationwide launch, rural clinics report that the model flags almost every patient, and a regulator asks the network to explain why individual patients are flagged. A data review notes that rural clinics joined the scheduling system only last month. Which TWO actions address these problems BEST? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Retrain with data that represents rural clinics, and check accuracy separately for rural and city patients before relaunch
Keep the model unchanged, because high overall accuracy on city data proves that the model works equally well for every clinic
Train a much larger model on the same city data, because larger models generalize to rural patients without needing new data
Remove human review of the reminders, so that the model's decisions are applied faster and are no longer questioned by clinic staff
Use explainability methods that show which factors drove each prediction, so staff and the regulator see why a patient is flagged

stem: A three-person startup has packaged its web API, which serves several request routes, as a single container. Traffic is unpredictable: busy during European business hours and often zero overnight and at weekends. The founders have no Kubernetes or operations experience and do not want to manage servers. The investor agreement adds that hosting cost must fall to almost nothing when nobody is using the product, and the developers do not want to restructure the existing container into separate functions. Which option fits BEST?

choices.text: A Cloud Run service, which runs the existing container, scales with requests and removes all instances when traffic stops
Cloud Run functions, after splitting the API into separate event-driven functions that each handle one kind of request
A Compute Engine managed instance group with autoscaling, which keeps at least one virtual machine running at all times
GKE Autopilot, because Google manages the nodes while the team writes Kubernetes manifests for the container and its scaling

stem: A building-materials group has finished discovery and assessment for its move to Google Cloud. A desktop reporting tool is used by three people and duplicates dashboards the company already has in Looker. The billing system runs on a mainframe under a support contract that ends in two years, with penalties for early exit. A Java order application with a self-managed PostgreSQL database is stable, but the database team spends days each month on patching and backups. Leadership wants to avoid rewriting stable code this year. Which THREE decisions fit BEST? (Select THREE)

choices.text: Rehost the desktop reporting tool on a Compute Engine virtual machine so that its three users keep their current workflow
Replatform the order application, moving its database to a managed service such as Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL
Reimagine the order application as a new product, rewriting its code and database this year to gain agility
Refactor the mainframe billing system into microservices this year, accepting the contract's early-exit penalties
Retire the desktop reporting tool, moving its three users to the existing Looker dashboards
Retain the mainframe billing system until its contract ends, and plan its migration for that date

stem: A consumer-goods company's marketing data, several years of campaign records, sits in Amazon S3, while its sales data is in BigQuery. Analysts know BigQuery well and want to join the two for weekly campaign reports. The marketing contract forbids moving raw marketing records out of the other cloud, but aggregated results may be moved. The governance team adds a detail: analysts must not receive credentials for the other cloud; access should be granted on tables in Google Cloud instead. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Install AlloyDB Omni in the other cloud, load the S3 files into it, and give analysts that cloud's credentials for queries
Copy the S3 files nightly into Cloud Storage with Storage Transfer Service, then load them into BigQuery for the joins
Give analysts keys to the other cloud's own query service, and paste its results into spreadsheets beside BigQuery reports
Use BigQuery Omni with BigLake tables over the S3 data, and bring only aggregated query results into BigQuery

stem: A freight insurer wants to sell access to its risk-scoring capability to logistics platforms, and expects dozens of partners within a year. Product managers want tiered plans with different call limits, and partner developers must sign up and get keys without emailing staff. The scoring backend runs in another cloud provider and is frozen for two years; it only offers an older SOAP interface, while partners expect REST. The CFO asks for one Google Cloud product to deliver these goals without backend changes. Which option fits BEST?

choices.text: A rewrite of the backend as REST services on Cloud Run, with a hand-built website where partners request keys by email
Cloud Armor in front of the backend, with security policies that limit request rates and a separate rule set for each partner
Apigee API Management, with proxies that front the existing backend, enforce quotas, run a developer portal and package API products
Cloud Load Balancing with a global address, so partners reach the SOAP backend faster from every region worldwide

stem: A marketing agency runs a campaign site on Compute Engine, analytics in BigQuery and staff collaboration in Google Workspace. A customer list leaked last month. The investigation shows that the site's VMs were fully patched and Google's infrastructure was not compromised, but an employee had granted access to a BigQuery dataset to all authenticated Google accounts while testing. The board asks which party was responsible for the failed control and what the model says about each service. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The agency was responsible, because access policies and data are the customer's duty in every model, managed services included
Google was responsible, because BigQuery is a managed service and managed services make the provider responsible for dataset access
Responsibility was shared equally, because BigQuery sits between IaaS and SaaS and so each party owns half of every control
Google was responsible, because Google patches the Compute Engine guest OS and therefore owns all security of the workload

stem: A retailer's resource hierarchy has an organization node, a Development folder and a Production folder. Two years ago an administrator granted the legacy Editor role to the whole developer group at the organization level. The CISO now wants developers to keep working freely in development projects but to lose write access to production, and wants future development projects to get the same access automatically. A consultant notes that granting developers a read-only role on the production folder would leave them able to change production. Which TWO actions fix this BEST? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Grant the developer group a read-only role on each production project, because a lower-level role overrides the inherited Editor role
Grant the developer group predefined roles on the Development folder, so current and future development projects inherit the access
Create a custom role at the Development folder level, because folders are where custom roles must be defined for inheritance
Grant each developer the Owner role on each development project individually, so production is unaffected by the change
Remove the organization-level Editor grant, because allow policies are inherited by every folder and project below the organization

stem: An engineering firm hosts an internal project-tracking web application in Google Cloud. Its own staff already sign in with company Google accounts. About 200 contractors from partner companies have been given accounts too, and must use the application from their own laptops in many locations; their internet addresses change daily. Security wants each request allowed or denied based on the person's identity and context rather than network location, and wants to avoid giving contractors any broad access to the firm's internal network. Which offering fits BEST?

choices.text: Cloud VPN tunnels for every contractor, giving their laptops a connection into the firm's internal network for the application
Cloud Next Generation Firewall rules that open the application's port to the internet ranges of each partner company
Identity-Aware Proxy, which lets only authenticated users with the right IAM role reach the application through the proxy
Cloud Armor rules that allow only the contractors' known IP addresses, updated each morning when their addresses change

stem: A furniture retailer's finance team is choosing pricing models for three Compute Engine workloads. The ERP application servers run 24 hours a day at a steady size and will stay for at least three years. A test environment on N2 machines runs most of each month, but the project may be cancelled next quarter, so finance refuses any commitment for it. A nightly image-resizing job splits work into small pieces that are retried automatically if a machine disappears. Which THREE choices fit BEST? (Select THREE)

choices.text: A one-year committed use discount for the image-resizing job, so that nightly capacity is guaranteed whenever the job is started
A three-year committed use discount for the test environment, because it runs most of the month on the same machines
Spot VMs for the ERP application servers, because their steady daily usage makes preemption by Compute Engine unlikely
Spot VMs for the nightly image-resizing job, because its small retryable pieces tolerate preemption at any time
Sustained use discounts for the N2 test environment, applied automatically for running most of the month without a commitment
A three-year resource-based committed use discount for the ERP servers, matching their steady, long-term usage

stem: A university research lab runs simulations on Compute Engine VMs with GPUs in one project. Last term a script error launched many VMs over a weekend and consumed half the annual budget. The lab director wants a technical limit on how many GPUs the project can use and an automated response when spending crosses a threshold. A colleague suggests a spend cap budget, but the billing documentation lists which services spend caps currently cover, and Compute Engine is not among them. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: An alerts-only budget with email notifications to the director, because a budget alert stops Compute Engine VMs automatically
Committed use discounts for the lab's GPUs, because a commitment sets a maximum on what the project can spend each year
A spend cap budget scoped to Compute Engine for the project, which pauses all VMs as soon as costs reach the budget amount
Lower Compute Engine quotas for GPUs and VMs, plus a budget whose Pub/Sub notifications trigger an automated shutdown script

stem: A payroll platform has an internal SLO of 99.9 percent availability over a 30-day month, and its customer contract (SLA) promises 99.5 percent with service credits. This month a failed database upgrade already caused 30 minutes of unavailability, and no other downtime has been recorded. A product team wants to ship a large, risky release next week. The product director asks the SRE lead for the numbers before deciding. The company's error budget policy states that once less than half of the monthly error budget remains, releases are limited to reliability fixes. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The error budget is about 43 minutes, about 13 remain, so the policy limits releases to reliability fixes
The SLA has been breached and credits are owed, because 30 minutes exceeds the 99.5 percent allowance for the month
The monthly error budget is about 4.3 minutes, so the SLO was missed early and every kind of release must stop
The error budget is about 432 minutes, so 30 minutes is small and the risky release can go ahead as planned
